officialTitle: Atezolizumab for First-Line Treatment of Metastatic Nonsquamous NSCLC
subtypes: EGFR/ALK wild-type (primary population); EGFR/ALK-altered patients in ITT

design.notes: Three arms: ACP, BCP, ABCP. ABCP vs BCP compared before ACP vs BCP. WT population excluded EGFR/ALK alterations.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding atezolizumab to bevacizumab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel improve PFS and OS in first-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC?

pico.population: Chemotherapy-naive metastatic non-squamous NSCLC (primary analyses in EGFR/ALK wild-type)
pico.intervention: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel (ABCP), then atezolizumab-bevacizumab maintenance
pico.comparator: Bevacizumab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel (BCP), then bevacizumab maintenance
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: investigator-assessed PFS (WT and Teff-high WT) and OS (WT)

arms.label: ABCP
arms.regimen: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab plus carboplatin plus paclitaxel

publications.title: Atezolizumab for First-Line Treatment of Metastatic Nonsquamous NSCLC.
publications.label: Primary analysis (ABCP vs BCP)

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival was longer in the ABCP group than in the BCP group (8.3 months vs. 6.8 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.74; P<0.001)
the corresponding values in the Teff-high WT population were 11.3 months and 6.8 months (hazard ratio, 0.51 [95% CI, 0.38 to 0.68]; P<0.001).

Median overall survival among the patients in the WT population was longer in the ABCP group than in the BCP group (19.2 months vs. 14.7 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.96; P=0.02).

safety.sourceQuote: The safety profile of ABCP was consistent with previously reported safety risks of the individual medicines.

strengths: Randomised phase III with co-primary PFS and OS endpoints
Prespecified exploratory subgroups (PD-L1-low/negative, liver metastases, EGFR/ALK-altered)
limitations: EGFR/ALK-altered and liver-metastasis subgroup findings are not powered for definitive conclusions

clinicalImplications.text: Established atezolizumab plus bevacizumab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel as a first-line option for metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, with exploratory signals in subgroups such as liver metastases and EGFR/ALK-altered disease.

tumourBoardPearl.text: ABCP is the regimen often discussed for EGFR/ALK-altered patients after TKI failure — but that evidence is exploratory subgroup data.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 29863955. Total randomised N across three arms not printed in abstract; WT arm sizes (356/336) recorded per arm.
